intro: Long-term structural theses as of June 26, 2026. The KOSPI 'Black Friday' −5.81% session and Russell Reconstitution (NVDA #1 at $4.8T, MU/AMD fully Growth, SpaceX Russell 1000) mark a pivotal inflection in the AI semiconductor cycle. Near-term regime volatility (VIX 18.63, DXY 101.43, SPX 7,357 below 7,460 gate) does not alter structural 1-5 year theses. These ideas represent the core multi-quarter and multi-year positions underlying the daily tactical framework. The tactical entry framework (regime gates, stop levels) remains the vehicle for building into these structural theses — the ideas here describe WHY to own these over years, not when to add today.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.idea: NVIDIA is the dominant AI infrastructure platform for the 2020s. The Russell Reconstitution June 26 2026 confirmed NVDA as the world's largest company by passive index weight at $4.8T — a structural change, not a one-time event. Every passive dollar flowing into the Russell 1000/3000 now has its largest single allocation to NVDA.
ideas.why: H100/H200/B200/B300 GPU platform lock: hyperscalers (MSFT Azure, AMZN AWS, GOOGL GCP, META, Oracle) have committed multi-year capex to NVIDIA silicon with no competitive alternative at scale. CUDA ecosystem: 5M+ developers are trained on CUDA, creating switching costs that exceed hardware replacement cycles. NIM microservices and NVIDIA AI Enterprise create recurring software revenue on top of hardware. $80B buyback program and $0.25/share quarterly dividend (2,400% increase) signal management confidence in sustained free cash flow. Micron's $50B Q4 FY2026 HBM4 guide validates AI infrastructure spend is real, not hype.
ideas.driver: H3/H4 GPU architecture cycles (2027-2028); NIM/NEMO software platform attach rate increasing; inference silicon demand expanding beyond training; sovereign AI infrastructure spending (India, Japan, Middle East); continued hyperscaler capex guided forward 18+ months.
ideas.risk: US export control expansion cutting Chinese revenue (currently ~15% of total but declining); AMD MI400 series gaining meaningful share in inference workloads (not yet competitive at scale); custom silicon (GOOGL TPU, AMZN Trainium, MSFT Maia) displacing NVDA for a specific hyperscaler's workloads; regulatory action on CUDA monopoly.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc.
ideas.idea: SK Hynix is the structural winner of the HBM3E/HBM4 cycle. The company is the sole-source HBM3E supplier for NVIDIA H100/H200 and is months ahead of Samsung on HBM4 qualification for B200/B300. The KOSPI −5.81% 'Black Friday' June 26 event is tactical, not structural — it does not change the HBM supply/demand dynamic.
ideas.why: HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) is the primary AI chip memory tier — each H100 requires 80GB HBM3E, each B200 requires 192GB HBM3E. NVIDIA's B300/H3 roadmap requires HBM4 at 2x the bandwidth. SK Hynix has 18-month lead on Samsung for HBM4 qualification. The ADR program ($33B estimated) would give SK Hynix access to US passive capital channels — permanent demand from US-listed index ETFs. AAPL/MSFT consumer price increases citing memory costs confirm OEM pass-through, validating SK Hynix pricing power at every tier.
ideas.driver: ADR listing catalysis (SEC clearance expected imminently, underwriters BofA/Goldman/Citigroup/JPMorgan); HBM4 sole-source qualification for NVIDIA B300 platform; AI PC and on-device inference memory demand (LPDDR5X) adding a second growth vector beyond HBM; DRAM price recovery cycle into 2027.
ideas.risk: Samsung qualifies HBM4E on same schedule as SK Hynix — breaks sole-source pricing premium; KOSPI two consecutive closes below ₩2,540,000 stop — technical stop-out before structural recovery; ADR SEC clearance delayed beyond Q3 2026; US-Korea trade policy changes affecting semiconductor exports.

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.idea: Micron is the US-listed proxy for the HBM supercycle. The $50B Q4 FY2026 revenue guide and AAPL/MSFT price increases citing memory costs confirm MU is in the strongest demand cycle in semiconductor memory history. The Russell Growth reclassification at June 26 reconstitution permanently adds MU to the passive Growth channel.
ideas.why: Micron is the only US-headquartered HBM supplier — it benefits from any 'supply chain security' or 'CHIPS Act' dynamics that disadvantage Samsung or SK Hynix. HBM3E and HBM4 capacity is sold out through 2026. The $50B Q4 FY2026 guide is the strongest earnings beat in the 2026 AI cycle — not a beat vs consensus, but a step-change guide 40%+ above prior estimates. MU's inclusion in Russell 1000 Growth (IWF, VONG, SCHG) after the June 26 reconstitution creates permanent passive demand from ~$2T in Growth index ETF AUM.
ideas.driver: HBM4 mass production 2H 2026; DRAM pricing inflection (tight supply, accelerating demand from AI PC + inference + HBM); Q4 FY2026 earnings (September 2026) confirming $50B guide; MU potentially added to S&P 500 Top 10 weighting as market cap grows.
ideas.risk: Samsung price-cuts DRAM aggressively to regain share at the expense of margins; US-China trade war escalation reduces data center spending; Memory downcycle triggered by hyperscaler inventory digestion in 2027; Hot PCE driving rate increases that compress semiconductor multiples broadly.

ideas.name: Microsoft Corporation
ideas.idea: Microsoft Azure is the enterprise AI moat. The June 25 Xbox price increase citing memory costs is a signal — not a concern — that MSFT has pricing power across its entire product ecosystem. Azure OpenAI Service, Copilot 365, and the GitHub Copilot platform create the deepest enterprise AI distribution channel in the world.
ideas.why: Azure is the #2 hyperscaler growing faster than AWS on AI workloads. The OpenAI partnership gives MSFT exclusive commercial rights to GPT-5/6 on the Azure platform — every enterprise that builds on OpenAI builds on Azure. Copilot for M365 (1.4B Office users, 350M paid M365 users) is the largest enterprise AI distribution channel in history — the attach rate from free trial to paid ($30/seat/month) is accelerating. GitHub Copilot dominates developer AI tools (>1.4M paid seats growing 50%+ YoY). Price increases (Xbox, M365 enterprise) confirm MSFT can pass through cost inflation — rare in enterprise software.
ideas.driver: Azure AI revenue overtaking Google Cloud for AI workloads (2027); Copilot 365 attach rate inflecting to >20% of M365 base; AGI timeline acceleration benefits the OpenAI exclusivity agreement; Nuance DAX (healthcare AI documentation) reaching scale.
ideas.risk: OpenAI relationship deteriorates or exclusivity ends; GOOGL Workspace + Gemini gains enterprise market share; Antitrust action on Azure cloud bundling; AI CapEx cycle creates cost overruns that compress Azure margins.

ideas.name: Alphabet Inc.
ideas.idea: Alphabet is the cheapest full-stack AI megacap. Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra is a frontier model; Google Cloud (GCP) is the #3 hyperscaler; YouTube is AI advertising infrastructure; Waymo is the only robotaxi with commercial operations at scale. At current valuations, GOOGL is pricing in AI disruption to Search that has not materialized in revenue terms.
ideas.why: Google Search revenue grew 12% YoY in Q1 2026 despite AI Overview rollout — the feared 'AI kills Search advertising' narrative has not played out. Gemini Ultra is competitive with GPT-4o; Gemini 2.0 and 3.0 pipeline is intact. GCP has the cleanest AI infrastructure story: TPU v5 competitive for inference, Vertex AI gaining enterprise adoption. YouTube Shorts monetization is accelerating. Waymo is 18 months ahead of any competitor in Level 4 autonomous vehicles — ONE successful 10-city robotaxi launch changes the financial model completely.
ideas.driver: Search AI integration driving query monetization HIGHER (premium placements for AI answers); Waymo commercial launch beyond San Francisco and LA (Austin, DC in progress); Gemini Ultra enterprise adoption via Google Workspace; GCP AI market share gains from hyperscaler diversification.
ideas.risk: AI-native search (Perplexity, Claude.ai, ChatGPT) accelerates Search query displacement faster than GOOGL can monetize AI answers; EU Digital Markets Act compliance creates structural disadvantage in European Search; Antitrust remedy forces Chrome/Search unbundling; GCP loses enterprise accounts to Azure OpenAI lock-in.

ideas.name: Procure Space ETF
ideas.idea: STEP ASIDE near-term (through July 10 bond distribution clearance). Long-term: SPCX is the most concentrated public access to the commercial space economy — 40% of AUM is SpaceX-linked via Maxar, Planet, Rocket Lab, Aerojet, and the new SpaceX direct inclusion (Russell 1000 addition June 26). The $89B demand for $25B SpaceX bonds at 6.5-7% yield confirms institutional valuation thesis: SpaceX at $500B+ pre-IPO, Starshield DoD contracts, Starlink profitability.
ideas.why: SpaceX is the defining infrastructure company of the 2020s-2030s: Starlink has 5M+ paying subscribers, Starshield (military LEO) is DoD's strategic priority, Falcon 9 has 95%+ global commercial launch market share, Starship is the only HLV platform in commercial development. An SpaceX IPO (no announced date, but $500B+ implied valuation by bond pricing) would be the largest IPO in history and directly benefits SPCX as the most SpaceX-concentrated ETF. September 2 earnings could include first-ever SpaceX revenue disclosure in the proxy.
ideas.driver: SpaceX IPO announcement (most likely 2027-2028); Starship reaching full commercial operations; Starlink profitability confirmation ($4B+ revenue run rate); DoD Starshield contract awards; Mars mission timeline acceleration catalyzing valuation narrative.
ideas.risk: Bond distribution mechanics persist beyond July 10 (delays re-entry); Starship development setback (FAA license, Boca Chica regulatory action); SpaceX decides against IPO indefinitely; Competing launch providers (Blue Origin New Glenn, Rocket Lab Neutron) taking meaningful share; $150 ETF floor breaks on distribution pressure, forcing lower re-entry point.

ideas.name: Bitcoin / US Dollar
ideas.idea: Structural digital gold thesis intact — re-entry framework governs the tactical timing. BTC is at $59,397 (June 26, 11:02 UTC) with the re-entry clock inactive. The two-consecutive-UTC-close-above-$62,000 framework remains the entry gate. Long-term target: $120,000-$180,000 on the post-halving supply/demand cycle (April 2024 halving, full effect typically 18-24 months post-event = late 2025 to mid-2026).
ideas.why: Bitcoin's April 2024 halving cut block reward from 6.25 to 3.125 BTC — ~$5B/year of new supply removed at current prices. ETF flows (BlackRock IBIT, Fidelity FBTC, ARK 21Shares) have absorbed 3-5x daily new supply since January 2024. Sovereign treasury adoption (El Salvador confirmed, MicroStrategy $42B+, two additional nation-states rumored) reduces floating supply. The '$62,000 gate' framework protects against false breakouts — the declining session highs ($60,767 vs $61,967 prior session) suggest the current distribution ceiling is falling, consistent with near-term HOLD.
ideas.driver: Post-halving supply shock fully materializing (18-24 month cycle = late 2025 to mid-2026 peak); Spot BTC ETF net inflows resuming after risk-off period clears; Institutional treasury adoption accelerating; US Strategic BTC Reserve legislation (introduced, not passed); Re-entry clock activation ($62,000 two-day close).
ideas.risk: BTC drops below $50,000 (cycle low support) before re-entry clock activates — framework-defined exit; Regulatory action (SEC, CFTC, G7 coordinated action) targeting BTC specifically; Mt. Gox final distribution creating sustained sell pressure; Macro risk-off (global recession) correlating BTC with equities in a prolonged drawdown.
